artists.biography:
Paul Frederic Simon (born October 13, 1941) is a Grammy Award winning American singer-songwriter, poet and guitarist.
Simon's international fame and success began as part of the duo Simon & Garfunkel, launched in 1964 with musical partner Art Garfunkel. Simon wrote most of the pair's songs, including three that reached No. 1 on the U.S. singles charts: "The Sound of Silence", "Mrs. Robinson", and "Bridge Over Troubled Water". The duo split up in 1970 at the height of their popularity, and Simon began a successful solo career, recording three highly acclaimed albums over the next five years. In 1986, he released Graceland, an album inspired by South African township music. Simon also wrote and starred in the film One-Trick Pony (1980) and co-wrote the Broadway musical The Capeman (1998).

perplexity.description:
Paul Simon's Stranger to Stranger, released in 2016 on Concord Records, is his thirteenth solo studio album and stands out as one of his most adventurous works. Blending elements of rock, pop, folk, and world music, the album features experimental textures and rhythms, including the use of custom-made instruments designed by composer Harry Partch. Collaborations with Italian electronic artist Clap! Clap! further expand its sonic palette, resulting in a sound that is both innovative and deeply rooted in Simon’s signature songwriting style.

Stranger to Stranger marks Simon’s first studio album in over five years and is notable for its lyrical depth and musical risk-taking. It debuted at No. 1 on the UK Albums Chart, making Simon, at age 74, the oldest male solo artist to achieve that feat, and reached No. 3 on the US Billboard 200. The album received widespread critical acclaim for its creativity and craftsmanship, cementing its place as a standout in Simon’s later discography.
